What's visible here is a `git-repository` being opened, which traverses the object database to get an idea on how to configure itself suitably. This traversal uses `jwalk` in parallel mode, which seems to get trapped into a loop. I am aware of `jwalk` implementing a rayon bridge which seems to have side-effects if rayon only has one thread. The reason this triggers seems to be that the `jwalk` crate by default uses the global thread queue, [which is configured by starhip](https://github.com/starship/starship/blob/1b5cc0cfdabfdbd89b8815a82b265c2a72862afb/src/main.rs#L249:L249) to use one thread. `jwalk` has a special mode for single-threaded operation which skips `rayon` entirely, and ideally it would kick if it detects that the global rayon queue has only a single thread. This might be an avenue forward towards a permanent fix. Edit: It's not, whenever the global rayon queue is reconfigured to anything less than 6 on my machine it hangs. In the mean time, I am working on a way to turn off `jwalk` specifically without affecting other aspects of `gitoxide`, which currently isn't possible.
